title: Calendar chaos → everything fits
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 1,584,000 samples (33.0 s at 30 fps = 990 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 33-second app-launch bed at 118 BPM in Ab major that goes from overloaded to tidy. Frames 0-174 (chaos): overlapping calendar-alert pings at clashing rates (sine+2nd partial, pitches drawn from a whole-tone set so they clash), muffled notification buzzes, a ticking clock at 1.7 Hz against the grid, and a sub drone on Ab0 slowly swelling; a filtered-noise riser climbs from frame 120. Frame 174 (5.8 s): everything cuts to 6 frames of silence. Frame 180: logo hit: sub boom on Ab1, warm Abmaj9 bell-pad chord, glass shimmer. Frames 180-420: a light four-on-the-floor (soft round kick, shaker on 16ths, no snare) with a plucked arpeggio on Abmaj9 → Fm9 → Dbmaj7 → Eb6, and a soft sine-chime on frames 210, 270, 330 and 390 (typing / reorganising accents, rising Ab5, C6, Eb6, G6). Frames 420-840: full groove, a 1/8-note marimba ostinato and three bright callout 'pops' on frames 450, 540 and 630 (each a 2-note rising mallet interval, different every time). Frames 840-870: 1-bar riser. Frame 870: 'Everything fits' resolve on Abmaj9 with a gentle impact, groove continues sparser, final logo hit on frame 930, ring-out to 0 by frame 990. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.

metrics.note: Public out.wav downsampled to 32000 Hz for Workers ≤5 MiB; metrics from 48 kHz master.

notes: App-launch bed: clashing calendar pings cut to silence at 5.8 s, then Ab-major four-on-floor with plucks, chimes and callout pops.
